title: Merging SpaceX and Tesla would be a "good idea," Musk says
gist: On SpaceX's Q3 earnings call, Musk said merging SpaceX and Tesla would be a good idea, with independent special committees already formed at both companies. Berger notes the combined entity would center on AI compute and would give Musk far more voting control.

insights.claim: Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call that merging SpaceX and Tesla would be a good idea, subject to shareholder support, and that special committees of independent directors at both companies are discussing it with no agreed terms.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A formal process exists, but a deal is not agreed and approvals are uncertain.
insights.quote: “Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,”

insights.claim: Musk said at least 50 percent of all Tesla shareholders, not only voting shares, would have to approve a merger, a high bar given expected valuation disputes.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Approval risk centers on Tesla shareholders, who may resist the valuation terms.

insights.claim: The merger faces scrutiny from US regulators and from political leaders already wary of Musk's power.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Regulatory timing adds uncertainty to any deal and to both stocks.

insights.claim: Musk justifies the merger by cooperation on superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab, robotics, mass to orbit with Starmind, and connectivity.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Management frames the combined company as a vertically integrated AI infrastructure play.
insights.quote: There’s lots to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab

insights.claim: Berger argues both companies are transitioning into AI: SpaceX expects most future revenue from orbital data centers for AI computing, while Tesla's future lies in self-driving cars, robots and industrial hardware, so a combined firm would deprioritize Mars and mass-market EVs.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Valuing the combined company on AI compute exposure rather than launch or auto fundamentals changes the investment case.
insights.quote: Less Mars and cars—and more silicon.

insights.claim: Musk holds over 82 percent of voting power in SpaceX but only about 20 percent in Tesla, so a merger could give him majority voting control of a larger combined company, depending on valuations; the companies were valued at about $2 trillion and $1.5 trillion.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Governance dilution for Tesla minority holders is a key second-order effect.

insights.claim: SpaceX acquired xAI in February and went public in June in the largest IPO on record, suggesting consolidation of Musk's holdings is already well advanced.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A Tesla merger would be the third step in a sequential consolidation pattern.
